events.label: Summer 2022: what Barbara does after Kieran's fall.
events.description: What she does with the guilt of having handed him a key without a map, and of having said nothing in February, is drawn from cut.barbara.2022.after.
events.region: Avebury Trusloe and the Ridgeway, Wiltshire

events.label: August 2022: Barbara goes to Laura herself.
events.description: Something none of the named options held (the remainder was drawn). Barbara, who has never met Laura, takes the bus into Swindon on a weekday while Kieran is at the Hart and knocks on the Wood Street flat. She leaves the car at home, because the car is where she composed the three sentences in February. She knows the flat from the lardy cake he once brought…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: September 1969: Barbara is let into the trade.
events.description: A new manager signs her on as an electrical apprentice after she beats every boy in the test; her father says nothing and gives her his screwdrivers.
events.region: The railway works, Swindon

events.label: Late October 2019: where Barbara's attention goes as she decides to send the card.
events.description: Her own state as she decides to send the card to the clerk who could not say how old the system was: among her wants to leave something to someone who could see it, to be credited, to verify and to be free, where her attention goes.
events.region: Avebury Trusloe, Wiltshire

events.label: A weekday in August 2022: Barbara takes the bus into Swindon.
events.description: From the stop outside the Red Lion she takes the bus into town for the first time in two years. She has not asked anyone for anything since 1986; she is going to give something that is not money, and she does not know how. She rehearses nothing, because rehearsing is what she did in February.
events.region: The bus from Avebury into Swindon

events.label: 2013: Barbara buys her first coins on retiring.
events.description: About a hundred dollars a coin; she keeps the keys on paper in a biscuit tin and never sells.
events.region: Avebury Trusloe and the Ridgeway, Wiltshire

events.label: Barbara's inner perspective root: wants, beliefs and appraisals attributed to them, never…
July 2022: Kieran tells Barbara the rest on a walk, and she names the key she gave withou…
events.description: Kieran walks with Barbara and tells her the rest. She does not laugh or mention casinos. She walks a long way without speaking, faster than him, with the collie trotting to keep up. At the long barrow she stops and puts her hand flat on a stone. She says, "I gave you a key, and not a map." He says it is not her fault. She answers that she did not say it was…
events.region: The Ridgeway above Avebury

events.label: 1969 to 1986: Barbara knows Ron Hale in the works.
events.description: Kieran's grandfather Ron Hale, a fitter in the boiler shop, is one of the few men who call the new girl apprentice Barbara from her first week. She remembers his big hands and that he whistled Elvis. She tells Kieran on their first walk in September 2020, when he says his grandad was in the works.
events.region: The railway works, Swindon

events.label: Autumn 2022 onward: Barbara teaches Kieran the map.
events.description: After her visit to Laura and the conversation it opened, Barbara starts, unasked, to explain on their walks how the systems he fell through work: the clearing file by file, why the part she wrote waits, what a key is and what a map is.
events.region: The Ridgeway above Avebury

events.label: The February 2022 walk, at the barrow: Barbara nearly says it.
events.description: She has the whole of it ready: the tent and the guy ropes, the sister token, the arithmetic. What stops her is the other name in it. Half the money is Laura's, Laura is not there and has not asked her, and Barbara, who spent seventeen years in the works being talked about by men who never said it to her face, has never discussed a woman's money behind her b…
events.region: The Ridgeway above Avebury

events.label: Childhood in a Rodbourne railway family, 1953-1969.
events.description: Her father a boilermaker at the works; she mends the family radio at ten and wants to be an electrician, which nobody takes seriously.
events.region: Rodbourne, Swindon

events.label: The works, 1969-1986.
events.description: One of very few women apprentices; the men call her Babs and she answers only to Barbara; a qualified electrical fitter by 1974; unmarried by choice; a long friendship with a woman draughtsman.
events.region: The railway works, Swindon

events.label: The bureau, 1988-2013.
events.description: Twenty-five years writing and maintaining clearing software in COBOL at a Reading bureau; the one who knows why the file stopped; never promoted past senior analyst; credited in no document.
events.region: Reading, Berkshire

events.label: Retirement and bitcoin, 2013-2019.
events.description: A cottage at Avebury Trusloe; walks on the Ridgeway; bitcoin bought in 2013 at about a hundred dollars and held through every crash; a quiet life with a laptop and a dog.
events.region: Avebury Trusloe and the Ridgeway, Wiltshire

events.label: The story years, 2019-2023.
events.description: The exit from the Hart, the card, the friendship with Kieran, his fall, her guilt.
events.region: Avebury Trusloe and the Ridgeway, Wiltshire

events.label: 2011: Barbara reads the bitcoin paper.
events.description: Nine pages that describe a ledger nobody can switch off. She reads it three times on the train to Reading and thinks: this is the part that waits, done properly.
events.region: Reading, Berkshire

events.label: A walk in December 2022: Barbara rereads the night Kieran logged off.
events.description: Kieran tells her about the guild and the raid he left in 2010. Barbara says that in the works, when the hooter went, a man put his tools down and went home, and nobody called it deserting: he went to work; it was the first grown-up thing he did.
events.region: The Ridgeway above Avebury

events.label: 1987-1988: Barbara retrains as a programmer.
events.description: A year of evening classes in COBOL at the technical college, paid for with her redundancy money; the only woman over thirty in the class; first in the exam.
events.region: Swindon

events.label: A Sunday in February 2022 on the Ridgeway: Kieran tells Barbara the deposit is in the sta…
events.description: They walk from the car park above Avebury towards the long barrow. He tells her, pleased, about twenty percent in a dollar. She stops walking. What she does is drawn from cut.barbara.2022.response.
events.region: Avebury Trusloe and the Ridgeway, Wiltshire

events.label: Barbara's state in February 2022, when Kieran tells her where the deposit is.
events.description: She has walked with him most months for eighteen months and likes him more than she expected. She thinks everything that is not bitcoin is a casino and the stablecoin a confidence trick with a formula. She believes in adults choosing their own risks and has spent her life refusing to be anyone's mother. Under that, for the first time, is the thought that sh…
events.region: Avebury Trusloe and the Ridgeway, Wiltshire

events.label: The February 2022 drive home: the three sentences Barbara does not say.
events.description: On the A4361 with the collie asleep on the back seat she composes them exactly. One: a dollar held up by guy ropes is a tent, and tents come down in weather. Two: take Laura's half out tomorrow, whatever you do with yours. Three: I gave you that card, so I get a say. She says none of them to anyone, because she has never been anybody's mother.
events.region: The road from Avebury to Swindon

events.label: The February 2022 walk: Barbara says it is his choice and nothing more.
events.description: Barbara stops on the track above the long barrow, looks at the barrow for a while, and says: that's yours and Laura's to decide. She says nothing else about it all afternoon. She talks about the men who dragged the stones and about the dog. On the drive home she thinks of three sentences she could have said and says none of them, because she has never been …
events.region: Avebury Trusloe and the Ridgeway, Wiltshire

events.description: Deepest want: to be believed and credited for what she knows and built.

events.description: Learned want from 1986 and 2008: verify, do not trust; a key nobody can switch off.

events.label: September 2020, on the first walk: Barbara quotes the biologist.
events.description: On the Ridgeway above the stones Barbara tells Kieran what a biologist she heard on the radio said: that we have Palaeolithic emotions, medieval institutions and god-like technology. She adds what she takes for a fourth thing: a phone in your hand at three in the morning.
events.region: The Ridgeway above Avebury

events.label: 30 July 2021: the last car leaves the line.
events.description: Kieran's father works the final shift, brings home his hi-vis vest and a commemorative mug, and puts the mug in a cupboard.
events.region: South Marston, Swindon

events.label: The car plant on the old airfield at South Marston
events.description: Engines from 1989 and cars from 1992; Kieran's father worked there from 1992. Its closure was announced in February 2019 and production ended at the end of July 2021.
events.region: South Marston, Swindon

events.label: 2002-2008: the car plant's steady years.
events.description: Full shifts and overtime; his father stops worrying aloud about the plant until the 2009 recession.
events.region: South Marston, Swindon

events.label: November 2019 to March 2020: the card behind the bus pass.
events.description: The white card rides in Kieran's wallet every day behind his bus pass, soft at the corners by March.
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: Barbara's card: a white index card with twelve words in her handwriting, and the wallet t…
events.description: Twelve words written in capitals in blue biro, posted to Kieran at the Hart on 1 November 2019 with a note: there is fifty pounds behind these; it is yours; go and look. The words are a recovery phrase for a wallet holding 0.0071 bitcoin. Kieran keeps the card behind his bus pass.
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: A typical clearing cycle at the Hart.
events.description: The outgoing file is built at ten at night and submitted; overnight the scheme processes it; at seven the exceptions queue shows what failed and why: a closed account, a mismatched name, a fraud flag. Nothing moves at weekends. The failure mode is a file that does not arrive and a day of payments that wait.
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: The interbank clearing system that the Hart's payments run through
events.description: Automated clearing designed for magnetic tape in the late 1960s: files submitted on day one, processed on day two, settled on day three, nothing at weekends. Barbara wrote software for it at a Reading bureau from 1988 to 2013, including the part that holds a payment while it waits. Since 2008 a faster scheme has moved single payments between banks in second…
events.region: Britain

events.label: The rota on the fridge.
events.description: Laura's shift pattern printed each month and held to the fridge by a magnet from Weymouth; it tells Kieran when she will be asleep, awake or gone.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Kieran and Laura's rented flat in Old Swindon
events.description: Two rooms and a spare room above a shop on Wood Street: the fridge with Laura's rota on it, the spare room where Kieran works the batch and farms at night, the kitchen table where the card is first read and where the truth is eventually told.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: June 2021: the Hart decides to block payments to several crypto exchanges.
events.description: After regulator warnings and a run of scam losses the board blocks card and bank payments to several exchanges. Kieran, who knows why payments fail, is seconded to the project that builds the block.
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: The week of 9 May 2022 at the Hart: the fraud lines fill.
events.description: Customers who moved savings into crypto, some through the very workarounds Kieran used, call about money that is gone. Staff from payments are pulled onto the phones.
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: The White Hart Building Society (invented): a mutual savings and mortgage society
events.description: Founded in 1868 by railwaymen pooling savings in a White Hart inn to buy houses; now about 1,100 staff, a head office and payments operations in west Swindon. Its day is set by the clearing cut-offs; in 2021 it decides to block payments to several crypto exchanges.
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: March 2023, on the Ridgeway: Kieran laughs a beat late.
events.description: When Laura makes her first joke about the deposit and Barbara laughs, he laughs a beat late. Under the laugh is the oldest fear the book gives him, of being outside the fire, still there at the moment he is let back in.
events.region: The Ridgeway above Avebury

events.label: September 2020, above the stones: Kieran thinks Barbara is wrong.
events.description: When Barbara says the biologist missed a fourth thing, a phone in your hand at three in the morning, Kieran thinks it is not a fourth thing but all three at once, and that the man on the radio missed nothing. He lets it stand, as he lets most things stand.
events.region: The Ridgeway above Avebury

events.label: Late August 2022, after the handover: Kieran answers.
events.description: At the kitchen table, when Laura stops at recommendation, Kieran answers without the scam-line voice, which he no longer has. He puts his hand next to hers, not on it, where she can take it or not, and says: we tell each other everything, every number, every time, even the boring ones; we start again, slowly; I'm sorry. The conversation goes on past one in …
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Friday 1 November 2019: where Kieran's attention goes when the card arrives.
events.description: His own state as the envelope with the twelve words arrives at the exceptions desk: among his wants to see the map, to matter, to be no trouble and to be safe, where his attention goes.

events.label: 2021: where Kieran's attention goes through the harvest year.

events.description: At nine there is a Teams call to mark the block going live, nine faces in nine spare rooms. Harriet from Compliance, new and serious, shares a bar chart of the year's scam losses and tells them about a widow in Highworth who sent her savings to a man she met on an app: we're seeing a lot of harm, she says, and, Kieran, you know what that looks like better t…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street
participants: Harriet, from Compliance at the Hart

events.label: Monday 21 October 2019, 3.40 pm: Kieran's scam-check call to Barbara.
events.description: He reads the script: has anyone contacted you and asked you to move your money, have you been promised returns. She laughs, answers every question and then asks hers: how old is the system he works in, and who could switch it off? He finds he does not know. She asks his name. The payment is released at 4.55. She asks which desk he is on; he tells her: payme…
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: Friday 1 November 2019: the letter with the card arrives at the exceptions desk.
events.description: An envelope addressed in capitals to Mr K. Hale, Payments Exceptions, Third Floor, White Hart House. A white card, twelve words, and a note: there is fifty pounds behind these; it is yours; go and look. He must declare gifts from customers: it is in the handbook and in the refresher course Compliance runs every October in the training room, which he sat a f…
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: October 2022 onward: Kieran tells nobody at the Hart.
events.description: He sits through Harriet's refresher course in the training room, the same October course with the same cartoon, with the card in his wallet, watches the cartoon of the man holding chocolates under a red cross, and does not put his hand up. He never tells Harriet about the card, the app or the three payments of eight thousand pounds; in March 2023 he says on…
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: October 2022: whether Kieran tells Compliance.
events.description: Since November 2019 he has kept a customer's gift undeclared, in 2021-22 he walked round the block he built; and in January 2022 he moved the deposit out in three payments kept under the queue's threshold. Harriet from Compliance, who said we are seeing a lot of harm and meant it, runs the refresher course in October. What he does is drawn from cut.kieran.2…
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: October 2022, the training room: Kieran does not put his hand up.
events.description: Harriet runs the same refresher course with the same cartoon of a man holding chocolates under a red cross. Kieran sits through it with Barbara's card in his wallet, thinks of the app and the three payments of eight thousand pounds, and does not put his hand up.
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon
participants: Harriet, from Compliance at the Hart

events.label: 9 to 13 May 2022: Kieran holds everything.
events.description: Four nights at the spare-room desk with the Sharehouse open on one screen and the price on the other. He reads the mechanism again and understands exactly why a run feeds itself. He does not sell at ninety cents, or sixty, or twenty. Laura is on nights; the rota says so. By Friday the deposit is worth about three thousand pounds and falling.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: 9 to 13 May 2022: Kieran watches the peg break.
events.description: Four nights at the spare-room desk. The stablecoin slips below a dollar on 9 May; the Sharehouse says it always comes back; the founder's account says he is deploying capital; Kieran reads the mechanism and understands it perfectly. What he does is drawn from cut.kieran.2022.depeg_response.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: A Sunday in January 2022: Kieran asks and Laura leaves it to him.
events.description: At the kitchen table, with the rota on the fridge behind her, he says he wants to move the deposit somewhere it will earn twenty percent before they buy in the summer. She is marking dates on the calendar and does not look up for long. You're the one who knows about money, she says. Do what you think. He does not explain what a stablecoin is, and she does n…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: January 2022: the house deposit goes into the stablecoin's savings protocol.
events.description: Twenty-four thousand pounds, fifteen of it Laura's, leaves the Hart through a payments app and becomes stablecoin earning about twenty percent. He moves it in three payments of eight thousand pounds on three days, from the joint savings account to his own account in the app, because he knows to the pound what drops a payment into the exceptions queue: he ha…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Autumn 2022 to March 2023: where Kieran ends up.
events.description: What he does with his job, with the game and with the mind that took him in is drawn from cut.kieran.2023.end.
events.region: Swindon and the downs

events.label: Autumn 2022 to March 2023: Kieran stays at his desk by choice, with open eyes.
events.description: He stays on the payments-exceptions desk at the Hart. The routine is the same and he is not: he knows how old the machine is and what runs under it, he knows what the new machine did to him, and he keeps Barbara's card with its small balance behind his bus pass. When a flagged transfer to a crypto exchange comes up he makes the call, reads the script, and t…
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: July 2020: six thousand pounds of his own savings go in.
events.description: His half of a holiday fund that the pandemic cancelled. He tells himself it is his money and not the deposit, which is true.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: September 2020: Kieran and Barbara meet in person and walk the Ridgeway.
events.description: She emails him from the address on her letter, which he answered in March with a single line. They meet in the car park above Avebury in September 2020, the month of the rule of six. She is smaller than her voice and walks faster than he does.
events.region: Avebury Trusloe and the Ridgeway, Wiltshire

events.label: August 2020: Kieran finds the Sharehouse.
events.description: A month after his first stake, the week the yam breaks, a link in a forum thread about a token named after a vegetable leads to a chat server of a few thousand anonymous farmers awake in every time zone. They answer his questions at three in the morning and call him Kez after his wallet name. It is the first band that has needed him since the guild.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: Summer 2020: three clocks in the spare room.
events.description: He sets alarms for three and five and learns which pools thin at which hours. There are three clocks in the spare room now: his body's, which wants to sleep at eleven; the Hart's, which sends the file at ten and brings it back at seven; and the pools', which never stop. He starts living by the third. He does not see until much later that the crop is farming…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: A Sunday in September 2022: his father drinks from the plant mug.
events.description: His father has work as a caretaker at a primary school in Penhill and drinks his tea from the commemorative mug at last. He says that Dave Pritchard from the plant lost his redundancy on that bitcoin. Kieran says only that he knows, and does not say how: the call was a customer's. Then he tells his parents about the deposit. His mother, Sue, asks Laura, not…
events.region: Penhill, Swindon

events.label: August to October 2021: Kieran pays his parents' rent.
events.description: Three months of rent from his gains, August to October, until his father's redundancy money comes through, late because the plant counts his years from 1995, when he was made permanent, until the union wins back his three agency years from 1992, while his father looks for work at fifty-nine. His father thanks him once, in the car, without looking at him. It…
events.region: Penhill, Swindon

events.label: Thursday 12 May 2022: Kieran is afraid of the Hart.
events.description: When the fraud lines fill with customers who lost their savings, some through the same app he used to walk round the block, he is afraid of his employer for the first time: all morning he waits for someone from the fraud team to come down to the third floor with a printout of three payments of eight thousand pounds and his name at the top. Nobody comes. The…
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: 2010-2012: Kieran becomes no trouble.
events.description: He learns the payments floor fast, volunteers for the early shift, never argues with a manager, and is praised for it. He stops seeing the guild; nobody on the floor knows he once ran forty people across Europe.
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: Spring 2001: Kieran's grandfather Ron dies.
events.description: Ron, a works fitter until 1986, dies at seventy-four of a stroke. Kieran, eleven, keeps his brass works tally token. After the funeral nobody talks about the works any more.
events.region: Penhill, Swindon

events.label: A night in May 2010: Kieran logs off in the middle of a raid.
events.description: The night before his first shift at the Hart, twenty-five of the guild's forty are on voice chat, four minutes into the hardest fight of the expansion. The tank goes down; the healers are shouting; Kieran is calling it. He says: Sander, you've got it. And he logs off. He never logs in again, and the guild falls apart within a month. What he learns is not th…
events.region: Kieran's bedroom in Penhill, Swindon

events.label: 2021: the harvest year.
events.description: Kieran farms through the night, answers newcomers in the Sharehouse at three in the morning, watches six thousand pounds become thirty-eight and then seventy-one thousand on the screen, builds the Hart's crypto-payment block by day and pays his parents' rent after the plant closes.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: A night in November 2021: Kieran opens the folder called HOUSE.
events.description: With Laura asleep through the wall between two nights, Kieran opens the laptop they share to pay the electricity, and her folder called HOUSE is on the desktop, where it has been for a year. He has never opened it. He opens it: three houses, the listings saved, a spreadsheet of the mortgage at four rates, and a document called DEPOSIT with one line, updated…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Kieran's inner perspective root: wants, beliefs and appraisals attributed to them, never …
Saturday 28 May 2022, in the porch: Kieran says it is nice.
events.description: Standing in the porch of the house Laura wants, knowing the deposit is worth three hundred and forty pounds, Kieran thinks: now, here, before she sends the email; he says: it's nice, and, when she says she will email the adviser on Monday: Monday, yeah. He holds the door for the agent. In the car, when she says it will be better once they are in, he says it…
events.region: A three-bed semi in Wroughton, Swindon

events.label: March 2023: a flagged transfer, and Kieran's call.
events.description: A saver in her twenties moving her savings to one of the exchanges the Hart's block never covered trips the scam rules. Kieran reads the script, then asks what Barbara once asked him, and something of his own: whether she knows how old the thing she is leaving is, and how new the thing she is going into, and who she will tell if it goes wrong. He understand…
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: November 2021: Kieran likes the number.
events.description: At the peak he likes it, more than he would admit: some nights he opens the app only to look at seventy-one thousand pounds, and feels it in his shoulders like a warm bath.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Late 2022 onward: Kieran's reading of 2010 begins to change.
events.description: He has told himself the story of the logoff one way for twelve years: desertion. After Barbara's reading he is not sure he believes the other way, but the loyalty that kept him in the hold, never leave a band while it is losing, loosens a little.

events.label: Evening of 12 March 2020: Kieran types the twelve words in.
events.description: At the kitchen table in the flat, with the news on about the crash, he downloads a wallet app, types the words, and presses his thumb to the glass to confirm. The balance rises: 0.0071 bitcoin, about twenty-eight pounds. Then he finds the public ledger and the transaction that sent it to him, and the transactions behind it, branching back through thousands …
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: September 2021: his mother asks about the rent money.
events.description: In the kitchen in Penhill, with the door shut, his mother, Sue, asks whether the rent money is that bitcoin. He says it is savings. She says: well, be careful. He says he is.
events.region: Penhill, Swindon

events.label: March 2023: Kieran says one true thing about himself on a Hart line.
events.description: It is a small step over the line he drew between home and the Hart: nothing about the card or the payments, only that he bought and lost, but on a recorded line, to a customer, where the Hart can hear it. For a week he half expects someone from Quality to come down to the third floor with a transcript. Nobody does. Nobody listens to the calls that go well.
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: January to September 2022: what happens to Kieran's own stake.
events.description: His own money stays where it was, in the farm tokens and their pools: about 45,000 pounds in January 2022, about 13,000 on 9 May as everything falls with the stablecoin, about 6,000 by mid-June. It was never enough to replace the deposit. In September he sells what is left, about 5,200 pounds, and pays it into the joint account.
events.region: Online

events.label: Childhood in Penhill, 1990-2002.
events.description: A council-built house in Penhill; his father on shifts at the car plant, his mother a care assistant; his grandfather Ron, a works fitter until 1986, tells stories about the hooter. Kieran is quiet, clever with systems, and happiest drawing maps of invented places.
events.region: Penhill, Swindon

events.label: The game years, 2002-2010.
events.description: From twelve he plays an online role-playing game every night; at sixteen he leads a raiding guild of forty people across Europe who depend on his timetables. Middling GCSEs, a college course dropped, two years in a call centre. The guild is the first band that needs him.
events.region: Penhill, Swindon, and online

events.label: The Hart, 2010-2019.
events.description: Payments floor from May 2010; exceptions analyst by 2014; meets Laura at a friend's thirtieth in 2014; the flat on Wood Street from 2016; saving for a deposit. Reliable, liked, no trouble; the week has one shape.
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: The story years, October 2019 to March 2023.
events.description: The white rabbit, the fall, the harvest, the break and the reckoning.
events.region: Swindon, Wiltshire

events.label: Thursday 12 May 2022, after lunch: the call from Mr Pritchard.
events.description: On the fraud lines, the day the dollar is worth twenty cents, Kieran takes a call from Dave Pritchard in Stratton, sixty-one, thirty years at the car plant, who put his redundancy money into the dollar that did not move: they said it was a dollar; can you get it back? You're a bank. Kieran does not let himself think of his father. His voice is the one he us…
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: November 2019 to March 2020: the card behind the bus pass.
events.description: He searches the words once on his phone and learns they are a recovery phrase; he does not type them in. The card makes the routine feel like a costume: every scam-check call now has a second voice in it. He does not tell Laura, the first thing in five years he has not told her.
events.region: White Hart House, the Hart's head office in west Swindon

events.label: 9 to 13 May 2022, at the decision: Kieran's own reasons for holding.
events.description: What holds him, as the peg breaks: fear of exile from the band and of making the loss real by selling, and love that has become loyalty to the Sharehouse. These are his reasons, authored in round 1 as the moment of the decision, not a reader's interpretation.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: January 2022, at the decision: Kieran's own reasons for moving the deposit.
events.description: What moves him, as he decides: love for Laura and the front door she wants, and fear that house prices in Wroughton are leaving them behind. These are his reasons, authored in round 1 as the moment of the decision, not a reader's interpretation.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Kieran's state in early January 2022, before the deposit moves.
events.description: The market is a third down from November; his seventy-one thousand is forty-five on the screen. House prices in Wroughton have risen faster than their deposit. His father has been out of work since July and pretends not to mind. The Sharehouse has spent December saying that the smart money is in safe yield now, twenty percent in a dollar that does not move.…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Kieran's state on the evening of 9 May 2022, as the peg starts to slip.
events.description: Three hours of sleep a night since the weekend. The deposit is the only money he has that is not already down seventy percent. The Sharehouse is loud and sure: it has always come back, the founder is buying. What he knows about the mechanism depends on what Barbara told him in February. He has not told Laura where the deposit is, or has, depending on Januar…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Kieran's state on 14 May 2022, the morning after.
events.description: The deposit is worth about three thousand pounds and still falling; his own stake is down more than ninety percent from November. He has not slept properly for a week. All that week at the Hart he has taken calls from customers who lost their savings, in the voice he used on Barbara. The Sharehouse has gone from certainty to jokes. Laura does not know; the …
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: November 2021 into the winter: what Kieran tells himself.
events.description: Not yet. At a hundred thousand it would be a surprise, and a surprise is not a secret. He tells himself this the night he closes her folder and most nights after, until the market falls far enough that the number stops being a surprise of any size.

events.label: May to July 2022: whether, when and how Laura learns where the deposit went.
events.description: The mortgage adviser wants statements by the middle of June. What Kieran does, and when Laura knows, is drawn from cut.kieran.2022.telling.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Mid-June 2022: five weeks of hiding, then the mortgage forces it.
events.description: For five weeks Kieran goes to work and comes home and says nothing. He takes scam calls in the day and checks a dead balance at night; he stands in the porch of the house she wants and says it is nice; he tells Mandy to tell her husband tonight and tells Laura nothing. When the mortgage adviser answers Laura's email asking for statements and she forwards it…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Mid-June 2022, the evening: Kieran tells Laura everything.
events.description: At the kitchen table, the rota on the fridge behind her, he asks her to let him get to the end, and tells her from the beginning, in order: the call and the card behind his bus pass; the spare room, the farms and the Sharehouse; seventy-one thousand pounds in November and the night he opened her folder called HOUSE and closed it again; January, the dollar t…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Winter 2022-23: three in the morning, once.
events.description: Woken at three for no reason, he goes through to the spare room out of old habit and opens the Sharehouse, where half the channels are empty. A newcomer asks whether it is too late to get in. He writes a long careful message about pegs and guy ropes and fires in draughts, deletes it, and writes: ask someone who loves you to sit with you while you decide. Th…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Learned want from the guild years: loyalty to whichever band needs him; leaving a band wh…
events.description: Learned want from the guild years: loyalty to whichever band needs him; leaving a band while it is losing is the one unforgivable thing.

events.label: Deepest want from 2014: a life with Laura and a front door that is theirs.
events.description: Deepest want from 2014: a life with Laura and a front door that is theirs.

events.label: Deepest want: to see the whole map, past the edges of the part he was given.
events.description: Deepest want: to see the whole map, past the edges of the part he was given.

events.label: Deepest want: to matter to people he can see, to be the one they needed.
events.description: Deepest want: to matter to people he can see, to be the one they needed.

events.label: Learned want from 2010: to be no trouble to anyone, the reliable one, as the way to stay …
events.description: Learned want from 2010: to be no trouble to anyone, the reliable one, as the way to stay safe and liked.

events.label: Learned want from 2021: to provide for his family with what he wins, as proof that the ga…
events.description: Learned want from 2021: to provide for his family with what he wins, as proof that the game was real.

events.label: Deepest want: to be safe, which his family taught him means a job for life and no trouble.
events.description: Deepest want: to be safe, which his family taught him means a job for life and no trouble.

events.label: Late August 2022: the conversation that did not happen in June.
events.description: That evening Laura says what she has not said: about the five evictions, about the deposit as a front door, about the five weeks. What the two of them do with it is drawn from cut.kieran_laura.2022.conversation.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: October 2022: the row about forty pounds.
events.description: Kieran forgets to mention forty pounds he spent on a game for the laptop, the first he has bought in twelve years. Laura finds it on the joint statement on a Thursday evening and turns the paper round: what's this? He says: it's forty quid, Lor. She says: every number, every time; you said that, at this table; and then: on the laptop, in the spare room. It …
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: September 2022 onward: they stay and rebuild in the open.
events.description: They open one joint account that both can see, put the rota and a spreadsheet on the fridge side by side, and postpone the house by two years. Kieran deletes the trading apps and tells Laura every number. Laura asks her friend Jade to swap shifts so she can have one Sunday a month off with him. They arrange the first exchange by the lockers, with Laura taki…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Saturday 28 May 2022: the viewing in Wroughton.
events.description: Laura has a Saturday off and books a viewing of the three-bed semi with the green front door and the porch, the house she found on her phone in January 2021, back on the market in May after its sale fell through; the sellers want a quick sale. She walks through it touching the door frames. In the porch she says: you could put your boots in here. Kieran, who…
events.region: A three-bed semi in Wroughton, Swindon

events.label: January 2021: where Laura's attention goes in the second wave.
events.description: Her own state in the worst weeks of the pandemic, beyond capacity on the unit and twenty minutes in the car before she comes up: among her wants to be competent, to have a home, to be cared for and to hold everything silently, where her attention goes.
events.region: The Swindon hospital and Old Swindon

events.label: A Sunday in January 2022: Laura says do what you think.
events.description: Asked by Kieran whether he can move their deposit somewhere earning twenty percent, Laura, marking viewings on the calendar on her seventh night shift in ten, says: You're the one who knows about money. Do what you think. Then: I trust you. She does not ask what it is.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Late August 2022: Laura gives Kieran the handover.
events.description: At the kitchen table with a notepad, as she sits at handover on the unit, Laura tells Kieran what the loss cost in the form she trusts: situation (the deposit is gone, fifteen thousand of it hers, the night shifts of the pandemic), background (five evictions, the bin bag at twelve, the deposit as a front door), assessment (he lied for five weeks, and before…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Laura's inner perspective root: wants, beliefs and appraisals attributed to them, never a…
September 2022: Laura asks Jade for the first Sunday swap.
events.description: By the unit lockers Laura asks her friend Jade to swap a Sunday shift. They compare their phones, Jade half into her coat. Jade can take the Sunday if Laura takes her Saturday. Laura agrees and starts offering more; Jade replies that it is a swap. Laura enters the exchange in green on the calendar.
events.region: The hospital unit lockers, then the rented flat on Wood Street

events.label: Mid-June 2022, at the kitchen table: what Laura learns besides the deposit.
events.description: Listening to Kieran tell it from the beginning, Laura learns more than where the deposit went: that a customer sent him a card before the pandemic and he told nobody; that the green line she saw climbing on his phone one morning in April 2020 was this; that for most of 2021 he had more on his phone than the deposit, seventy-one thousand pounds in November, …
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: September 2022 onward: Laura learns to say at home what she has always said at work.
events.description: On the unit she has always been the one who says the true thing first, to consultants, to families, to the dying; at home she held, as her mother did. After the handover at the kitchen table she starts saying it at home too, one Sunday a month and in the CHECKED column, and it is harder than any shift. Asking Jade for a day off with Kieran, Laura feels as t…
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: September 2009: Laura leaves home for nurse training.
events.description: A room in Oxford that is hers for three years; the first time she unpacks everything.
events.region: Oxford

events.label: 2012: Laura's mother remarries and has a secure home.
events.description: A council transfer and a kind second husband; Laura stops worrying about her mother's roof.
events.region: Highworth, Wiltshire

events.label: 2003-2009: Laura keeps her things in boxes.
events.description: In every room after the last move she keeps half her things packed. She decides at thirteen that she will own a front door nobody can take, and says so to nobody.
events.region: Highworth, Wiltshire

events.label: Childhood of rented rooms, 1991-2009.
events.description: Her mother works two jobs; they move five times before she is thirteen; she keeps her things in boxes. A steady, practical girl who looks after her younger brother.
events.region: Highworth and Swindon

events.label: Nurse training, 2009-2013.
events.description: A nursing degree in Oxford; she finds she is good in emergencies and bad at asking for anything.
events.region: Oxford

events.label: Nursing and Kieran, 2013-2020.
events.description: Wards, then intensive care from 2017; Kieran from 2014; the flat from 2016; saving towards a deposit, about four thousand pounds of the twelve by 2019; most of her fifteen thousand will be pandemic overtime.
events.region: The Swindon hospital and Old Swindon

events.label: The pandemic, 2020-2021.
events.description: Two waves on the intensive-care unit; night shifts; sleeping by day; the car outside the flat.
events.region: The intensive-care unit of the Swindon hospital

events.label: After the waves, 2021-2023.
events.description: Recovering; looking at houses in Wroughton; wanting to be looked after for once.
events.region: Old Swindon

events.label: Summer 2022: what Laura does once she knows.
events.description: What she does, and what it asks of her, is drawn from cut.laura.2022.response.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Summer 2022: Laura stays and holds it together in silence.
events.description: She listens, asks three practical questions, and goes to bed. In the morning she moves what is left into an account in her own name, picks up two extra shifts a week and writes to the adviser to withdraw the enquiry. She does not shout and does not cry in front of him. The conversation that should happen does not happen. The rota stays on the fridge.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: June to August 2022: the shame under Laura's silence.
events.description: Under the holding there is shame, not only anger. She was asked, and she said do what you think, and she did not look; she handed their front door to him the way her mother handed back keys. She cannot look at the fridge. The shame is why she says nothing: saying it would mean saying her own part, and she has no words for that until Barbara says hers.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: The morning after the handover: Laura says show me.
events.description: Laura gets up before him on her day off, opens the laptop at the bank with a pen in her hand, and says: right, show me; all of it; every account. He sits down beside her and shows her, account by account, and she writes it down. It is the opposite of do what you think, and it is how they choose to stay.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: Laura's state in early January 2022.
events.description: Four months out of the second wave and still sleeping badly. She wants to buy a house by the summer and has saved most of the deposit from overtime. She has not opened their savings app since the spring: Kieran is the one who knows about money, the way the monitors know about the patient. She is tired of being the one who holds everything.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: The January 2022 Sunday from Laura's side.
events.description: She hears twenty percent and a dollar and thinks of the monitors: numbers she does not have to check because somebody competent is watching them. It is her seventh night in ten. Saying do what you think is the first time in years she has put something down, and it feels, for a second, like rest.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: An April 2020 night on the COVID intensive-care unit.
events.description: Twelve and a half hours in a hood and gown on a unit running at about one and a half times its beds. With six others she prones a man of fifty-eight onto his front; she holds a phone to another man's ear so his daughter can say goodbye; the alarms sound all night like birds. She comes home at eight and finds Kieran asleep at the spare-room desk with the pho…
events.region: The intensive-care unit of the Swindon hospital

events.label: Deepest want: to be the one looked after, for once.
events.description: Deepest want: to be the one looked after, for once.

events.label: Deepest want: to be good at the work that keeps people alive.
events.description: Deepest want: to be good at the work that keeps people alive.

events.label: Learned want from her mother: hold everything together and say nothing.
events.description: Learned want from her mother: hold everything together and say nothing.

events.label: Deepest want: a home nobody can take away.
events.description: Deepest want: a home nobody can take away.

events.label: Summer 2020: Laura stops telling Kieran about her shifts.
events.description: There are no words for the unit that do not frighten him, so she tells him about the car park and the canteen. He stops asking. Each of them is alone with a screen: hers the monitors, his the charts.
events.region: Old Swindon and the hospital

events.label: January 2021: twenty minutes in the car, then houses on the sofa.
events.description: In January 2021, after an intensive-care shift, Laura sits in the car outside the flat for twenty minutes before coming up. Later she lies on the sofa scrolling through houses in Wroughton on her phone. It is the only thing she looks at that is not a monitor: a three-bed semi with a green front door, a garden and a shed.
events.region: Old Swindon

events.label: 2021: the battle between the old money and the new.
events.description: The regulator warns that people who buy crypto should be prepared to lose all their money; banks block payments to exchanges; exchanges buy football shirts and Tube adverts; inside crypto, bitcoin purists call everything else a casino and yield farmers call the purists dinosaurs; every side calls the others frauds. Kieran is on the front line of it twice a …
events.region: Britain and online

events.label: The COVID-19 pandemic in England, 2020-2022.
events.description: National lockdowns from 23 March 2020, November 2020 and January 2021; intensive-care units at or beyond capacity in April 2020 and January 2021; offices emptied and work moved to spare rooms.
events.region: England

events.label: The British response to payment scams and crypto, 2019-2022.
events.description: A voluntary code for reimbursing victims of authorised push-payment scams from May 2019, name checks on new payees from 2020, regulator warnings about crypto, a ban on selling crypto derivatives to retail customers from January 2021, and banks blocking or limiting payments to some crypto exchanges from 2021.
events.region: Britain

events.label: The town's week: the shape of ordinary time in Swindon.
events.description: Shift patterns inherited from the works and the plants, office hours set by the clearing cut-offs, the Thursday quiz, the Saturday town centre, Sunday lunch; the roundabouts and the M4.
events.region: Swindon, Wiltshire

events.label: The boom from late 2020 to November 2021.
events.description: Prices of bitcoin and of the decentralized-finance tokens multiply; bitcoin peaks near sixty-nine thousand dollars on 10 November 2021.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: Thursday 12 March 2020: bitcoin loses about half its value within a day.
events.description: Markets everywhere fall as the pandemic arrives; bitcoin trades near five thousand dollars at the low, down from about eight thousand the day before.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: The yield-farming summer of 2020.
events.description: From mid-June 2020 decentralized protocols begin paying their users in new governance tokens; farmers move money between pools chasing yields in the hundreds of percent; many of the new tokens are named after food.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: November 2022: a large crypto exchange collapses into bankruptcy.
events.description: Customer funds turn out to have been used by the exchange's trading firm; bitcoin falls to about a quarter of its peak.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: June 2022: a large crypto lender freezes withdrawals.
events.description: Contagion from the collapse reaches lenders and funds; customers cannot withdraw.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: The crypto market regime from the 2019 recovery to the 2022 collapses.
events.description: A market that never closes: the March 2020 crash, the yield-farming summer of 2020, the boom to November 2021, the slide through early 2022, the stablecoin collapse in May, the lender freezes in June and the exchange collapse in November 2022.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: The slide from November 2021 to May 2022.
events.description: Prices fall steadily; money moves from volatile tokens into stablecoins and their yields, especially the savings protocol paying about twenty percent.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: 9 to 13 May 2022: the algorithmic stablecoin loses its peg and its sister token collapses.
events.description: Large withdrawals from the savings protocol and sales of the stablecoin push it below a dollar; the mint-and-burn mechanism floods the market with the sister token, which falls to almost nothing within days. By 13 May the stablecoin trades at ten to twenty cents; by June at one or two.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: Spring 2020: the Sharehouse is founded.
events.description: A dozen yield farmers start a chat server as lockdown begins; by summer it has a few thousand members, channels named after food tokens, and a rule that nobody asks anybody's real name.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: The Sharehouse (invented): an online chat server of a few thousand anonymous yield farmers
events.description: Founded in spring 2020 as a yield-farming chat; a few thousand members in every time zone, a dozen who never seem to sleep, a language of memes and food tokens. It shares tips, losses, jokes and a belief that holding together is loyalty.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: Early June 2022: Mandy asks Kez whether to tell her husband.
events.description: Mandy, the dental nurse from the meetup, messages Kez privately: she lost eleven thousand pounds and her husband does not know. Should she tell him? Kieran, who has not told Laura, writes: yes. Tonight. Then he closes the laptop and does not tell Laura for another ten days.
events.region: Old Swindon: the rented flat above a shop on Wood Street

events.label: October 2021: the Sharehouse meets in the back room of a Swindon pub.
events.description: A regular in the Sharehouse turns out to live in Swindon; eleven members meet in the back room of a pub in Old Town, through a door marked PRIVATE FUNCTION past the toilets. They are ordinary: a dental nurse, a lorry driver, a sixth-former who should not be in a pub, a retired postman, a man from the council. Anyone can get pulled down the rabbit hole. In t…
events.region: The back room of a pub in Old Swindon

events.label: 9 to 13 May 2022 in the Sharehouse.
events.description: First certainty (it always comes back), then instructions (do not sell, that is what they want), then silence, then jokes, then goodbyes. By the end of May half the channels are empty.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: The stablecoin and its savings protocol (real in the background, unnamed in the story)
events.description: A dollar token that held its peg not with dollars in a vault but through a mint-and-burn arbitrage with a sister token: one stablecoin could always be swapped for a dollar's worth of the sister token. Its savings protocol paid about twenty percent. When confidence broke, redemptions minted more of the sister token, its price fell, and each swap bought less:…
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: How the stablecoin worked, 2020-2022.
events.description: Parts: the dollar token; the sister token; a swap that always let anyone trade one dollar token for a dollar's worth of the sister token and back; a savings protocol paying about twenty percent from reserves and new deposits. Capacity: the peg held while the sister token was worth more than the dollar tokens outstanding. Failure mode: when enough holders sw…
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: 9 to 13 May 2022: the spiral.
events.description: Withdrawals from the savings protocol and large sales push the token below a dollar; swaps mint the sister token by the billion; within four days the sister token is worth almost nothing and the stablecoin trades for cents.
events.region: Online: the Sharehouse and the chains, every time zone

events.label: The Avebury henge and stone circles
events.description: Raised by Neolithic farming communities between about 2850 and 2200 BC around a village that now sits inside the circle; the Ridgeway, used for at least five thousand years, runs along the downs above it. People dragged stones of up to forty tons there in order to gather.
events.region: Avebury, Wiltshire

events.label: About 2600 BC: the stones are dragged into place.
events.description: Farming communities drag sarsen stones of up to forty tons across the downs on sledges and rollers over generations, to make a place to gather at set seasons.
events.region: Avebury, Wiltshire

The passage later has Laura return from a night shift at seven and find Kieran at the laptop; he closes its lid. The partition and screen access shape what can be seen, without pr…

events.label: Physical arrangement and access within ev.kieran_laura.forty_pounds
events.description: Laura turns the statement so Kieran can read it. Later she sits with her back against the fridge; he sits beside her and she leans into him. The common wall of the fridge supports them both; the public spreadsheet is above them, unlike the previously private account check.

events.description: Kieran reaches across the table to place his hand beside Laura’s, without making contact. She neither takes nor withdraws her hand. Reach affords contact but does not constitute consent or reconciliation.
events.region: referent.twelve.place.kitchen

events.description: Laura’s shift includes coordinated bedside access and a later return to the Wood Street flat. Separate child Events identify these locations; no single coordinate represents both and no precise journey duration is inferred.

events.description: After the shift Laura stands at the spare-room doorway at home, sees Kieran asleep at the desk beside his lit phone, and then goes to bed.
events.region: referent.twelve.place.hallway

events.label: Physical arrangement and access within ev.walk.march_2023
events.description: The three walk on the Ridgeway near Avebury: Barbara leads with the collie, Laura is initially in the middle and Kieran behind. Later Laura takes his hand. The phone is in the car; the prose gives no exact parking place, route geometry, long-barrow destination or walking speed.
events.region: referent.twelve.place.ridgeway-route

events.label: Physical arrangement and access within ev.kieran.card_arrives
events.description: The paper recovery card arrives at the Hart office and is put behind the bus pass in Kieran’s carried wallet. The office is a place; the wallet is a portable container. Possession of the phrase does not establish another person’s knowledge of it.
events.region: referent.twelve.place.hart-floor

events.label: A Sunday in March 2023: Kieran, Laura and Barbara on the Ridgeway.
events.description: The three walk on the Ridgeway near Avebury: Barbara in front with the collie, too fast; Laura, who has never been up there, in new boots; Kieran behind. Laura asks why anyone would drag the stones so far; Kieran says people will do almost anything to gather. Barbara says he steals everything; Laura says: I know, he has got my deposit, the first joke she ha…
events.region: Avebury Trusloe and the Ridgeway, Wiltshire

events.label: The works hooter as the town's clock, 1843-1986.
events.description: For a hundred and forty years the hooter sounded the shifts across the town; people who never worked in the works set their clocks by it.
events.region: Swindon

events.label: The Great Western railway works at Swindon
events.description: For about a hundred and forty years the works made the town: sheds, hooter, shifts, the Friday pay packet, three generations of families. Kieran's grandfather and Barbara both worked there. It closed in March 1986.
events.region: The railway works, Swindon

events.label: Cultivation and its consequences, from about 12,000 years ago.
events.description: Farming produced surplus, storage, property, hierarchy, writing, money and debt. Time became the calendar of the harvest: the same work in the same field every season. Institutions grew to manage strangers who had to trust each other: temples, granaries, ledgers, kings, courts, and much later banks with double-entry books.

events.label: Programmable money: from the 2008 crisis and the first cryptocurrency to smart contracts,…
events.description: A ledger nobody owns, that never closes, where code replaces the clerk. It promised to route around the old institutions and instead reproduced most of their temptations at machine speed, in public, around the clock.

events.label: The networked and then pocketed computer, from the public internet of the 1990s to the sm…
events.description: Information, then attention, then money began to move at the speed of software. A phone in every pocket connected a forager's mind to millions of strangers at once.

events.label: Homo sapiens as mobile foragers, from about 300,000 to about 12,000 years before the pres…
events.description: For almost the whole history of the species people lived in bands of a few dozen inside a network of perhaps a hundred and fifty known faces. Trust ran on kinship, reputation and repeated meeting; wealth was what you could carry; a stranger was rare and a threat or a gift. The emotions the protagonist carries (fear of exclusion, hunger for status, the pull …

events.label: The global institutional order built mostly after 1944: a world of international money, t…
events.description: The global institutions people live inside took shape within roughly the last fifty to eighty years: post-war monetary agreements, the international lenders, card networks, interbank messaging, the floating dollar after 1971. They are younger than many living grandparents, and most people who depend on them have never seen how they work.

events.label: The slow institutions inherited from agrarian and early modern states: the bank, the ledg…
events.description: These are the medieval institutions of E. O. Wilson's phrase: they change on the scale of generations, settle disputes through intermediaries, open at nine and close at five, and remember everything in someone else's book.

lenses.name: Depleted or rested body
lenses.question: Is {subject} made from a rested body, a tired one, or a depleted one (short of sleep, stressed for weeks, running on habit)?

answers.meaning: Slept, fed, not under sustained stress; able to weigh the act.
Short of rest but still deliberating.
Weeks of short sleep or stress; the act runs on habit and on the group's lead.

lenses.why: The model holds sleep and exhaustion as processes (kieran.sleep_hours, laura.exhaustion) but no decision reads them. If depletion pushes choices towards habit and the group, then Laura's 'do what you think' on her seventh night of ten and Kieran's hold on three hours of sleep are partly the body's decisions, which changes where the story places blame and what it asks of the institutions that ran them down.
lenses.source: Stress physiology and sleep science (allostatic load: McEwen; sleep deprivation and decision-making).
lenses.trajectory: A person whose consequential acts cluster in depleted weeks is being decided for by their conditions; rest restores choice.

lenses.name: Exit, voice or loyalty
lenses.question: Facing decline or harm in a group or institution they belong to, does the person answer {subject} by exit (leaving), voice (speaking up to change it) or loyalty (staying and bearing it)?

answers.meaning: They leave: sell, close the account, move out, log off.
They speak up to change it: warn, complain, confess, tell the truth to the person who needs it.
They stay and bear it, silently, out of attachment to the group.

lenses.why: Kieran's loyalty to the band and Laura's silence are both loyalty without voice; Barbara exits the Hart in 2019, stays silent in February and then chooses voice in August. The lens predicts that loyalty without voice lets decline run to collapse, and that the story turns when someone moves from loyalty to voice. It also asks why Kieran exited the guild in 2010, the one exit he never forgave.
lenses.source: Albert O. Hirschman, Exit, Voice, and Loyalty (1970).
lenses.trajectory: Loyalty that never finds voice ends in a late, costly exit or in collapse; learning voice is a crossing.

lenses.name: Fear or love
lenses.question: Is what {subject} does primarily out of fear or out of love?

answers.meaning: Primarily out of fear: of loss, exclusion, being exposed, being left behind.

children.meaning: That what they have hidden will be seen, and they with it.
Losing what they hold: money, a home, a job, a place.
Being shut out of the band, the family or the fire: exclusion, being left.
That acting, selling or saying makes the loss or the mistake real.
That someone they love will be hurt, shamed, or will go.

answers.meaning: Primarily out of love: of the people and things they care for, or of themselves given to others.

children.meaning: For a particular person: a partner, a parent, a friend.
For the life they are making with someone: a home, a routine, the ordinary days.
For honesty itself: telling each other everything.
For what the work is for: the people it serves, the craft of it.

lenses.why: The same kinds of fear recur across four opened readings (the five weeks, the November night, the silence toward the Hart, Laura's handover) and the same kinds of love across two (the rebuild, the desk); fixing them as the lens's children keeps every later opening on one vocabulary.
lenses.trajectory: A life that moves from acting out of fear to acting out of love, or back, has changed at its root.

lenses.name: Gift, reciprocity or market
lenses.question: Is {subject} a gift (given without price, creating a bond and an obligation), reciprocity (a mutual arrangement among members), or a market exchange (a priced transaction between strangers)?

answers.meaning: Given without price; it binds giver and receiver and asks something back that is not money.
A mutual arrangement among members who owe each other: the mutual society, the shared deposit, the band's help.
A priced exchange between strangers, finished when it is paid.

lenses.why: Barbara's card, the rent Kieran pays his parents, the Sharehouse's three a.m. help and Barbara's lessons are gifts; the Hart was founded as reciprocity among railwaymen; the stablecoin is pure market. If the story's harm comes from treating a reciprocal thing (the shared deposit) as a market thing, and its healing from gifts (the visit, the lessons, 'pass the gravy'), the lens predicts which acts bind people and which dissolve them.
lenses.source: Marcel Mauss, The Gift (1925); Karl Polanyi, The Great Transformation (1944), on reciprocity, redistribution and exchange; David Graeber, Debt (2011).
lenses.trajectory: A life or an institution that moves from reciprocity to market loses the bonds that held it; one that learns to give re-forms them.

lenses.question: In {subject}, is this inner account the person's own reason (what actually moves them), an alibi (a story they tell themselves in its place, which lets them go on), or a recognition (something they come to see that they could not see before)?

answers.meaning: What actually moves the person, as they know it: a want, a fear or a love they would own if asked.
A story they tell themselves in place of the reason, which lets them go on without facing it.
Something they come to see that they could not, or would not, see before.

lenses.why: The story's inner Events hold what moves Kieran, what he tells himself instead (at a hundred thousand it would be a surprise, and a surprise is not a secret), and later what he comes to see (the phone as all three clocks at once; the logoff as going to work). An inner lens can show the arc from alibi to recognition, and set his own reasons at the deposit (love for Laura first) against what they are doing. Compared only with other inner readings.
lenses.source: Suggested by the operator in round 7: what Kieran tells himself, read against his own reasons.

lenses.name: Script or own voice
lenses.question: In {subject}, does the person speak or act in someone else's script (an institution's, a group's, a family's), in a borrowed form that carries their own words, in their own voice, or in silence?

answers.meaning: Someone else's words and order: the Hart's scam script, the Sharehouse's 'hold the line', the family's 'pass the gravy', the professional voice that hides the self.
A form taken from elsewhere (a handover, a fault report, a checklist) used to carry what the person could not otherwise say.
The person's own words, unscripted, at their own risk.
The act is saying nothing: a withholding of speech where something could be said (the undeclared card, the five weeks, holding it together without a word).

lenses.why: Kieran's arc runs from reading scripts (the scam-check questions, the Sharehouse's chants) to asking his own questions on the last call; the confession fails because the only voice he has is the scam-line one; Laura says the unbearable thing through the handover form; Barbara never uses anyone's script but hides behind her own rule. If voice is a process, the model predicts that a person can only repair in their own voice, and that borrowed forms (the handover) are how a person who has only ever held things together finds one. Revised: the first version had no answer for silence, and the silent acts (Kieran telling nobody at the Hart, Laura's two months, Barbara's February) fell to the remainder.
lenses.source: This story's own world (the Hart's scam-check script, the nurse's SBAR handover); kin to Bakhtin on authoritative and internally persuasive discourse, and to Goffman's front stage.
lenses.trajectory: A life that moves from script or silence to its own voice gains the power to repair and loses the protection of the script.

lenses.name: Shame or guilt
lenses.question: After {subject}, does the person carry it as shame (I am bad, so I must hide) or as guilt (I did something bad, so I can repair it)?

answers.meaning: The self is the problem: the person hides, goes quiet, performs normality, and cannot look at the act.
The act is the problem: the person can name what they did, own their part and repair it.
The act carries no moral weight for them at this moment.

lenses.why: The model has Kieran hiding for five weeks and Barbara saying 'I didn't say it was my fault. I said what I did.' If shame and guilt are distinct processes, hiding is predicted by shame and repair by guilt, and the turning point of the story is not the confession but the conversion of shame into guilt: Barbara's visit gives Laura and Kieran the grammar of guilt. It would also predict that Kieran's first scam-line voice in the confession is shame speaking.
lenses.source: The psychology of self-conscious emotions (Helen Block Lewis; June Tangney): shame targets the self, guilt the behaviour; shame predicts concealment, guilt predicts reparation.
lenses.trajectory: A person who moves from shame to guilt about the same act becomes able to repair it; one who stays in shame repeats the hiding.

lenses.name: The bit that waits
lenses.question: Does {subject} build in waiting before money or belief can move (a delay by design), slow it only by friction, or let it move at once?

answers.meaning: A delay is part of the design: a three-day cycle, a cut-off, a cooling period, a person who must be asked.
Nothing is meant to wait, but effort, paperwork or habit slow it.
Money or belief can move instantly, at any hour, by anyone.

lenses.why: Invented from Barbara's 'I wrote the bit that waits'. If waiting is a circuit breaker, the model predicts that systems which move at once fail in days (the stablecoin's spiral took four) while systems that wait fail slowly enough to be stopped, and that the old institutions' dullness is a safety feature, not only a cost. It also asks the same of people: Laura waits, Kieran cannot.
lenses.source: Invented for this story, from Barbara's line about the clearing code; kin to circuit breakers in market design and to cooling-off periods in consumer law.
lenses.trajectory: A system that removes its waiting gains speed and loses its brakes.

lenses.name: Wanting, bartering or standing
lenses.question: Is {subject} done in the child's stage (I want it, and I get it or I don't), bartering (the adolescent: conditional, a performance done to get a reaction or approval), or standing (the adult: unconditionally for what one stands for, even if disliked for it)?

answers.meaning: The child's stage: I want it, and I get it or I don't. The act is simply for the thing itself (money, comfort, rest, a home) and is judged only by getting it or not; nobody's reaction matters and no principle is at stake. Not the same as having wants: every stage has wants.
The adolescent's stage: conditional, a performance for a reaction: approval, belonging, being the reliable one, the loyal member, the one who holds everything, being no trouble.
The adult's stage: acting for what the person stands for, unconditionally, even at the cost of being disliked, blamed or alone.

lenses.why: Fear or love asks what moves an act; this asks what the act is for and on what condition. It can separate acts the model now reads alike: Kieran's reliability at the Hart and his loyalty in the Sharehouse may both be bartering for approval and belonging, which would predict that he holds in May 2022 because leaving would lose the reaction he performs for, not because he believes. Laura's silence may be bartering (holding everything to be the one who is relied on) or standing; Barbara's refusal to warn him may be standing for a principle that has hardened into a proxy. If true, the story's crossing is a movement from bartering to standing, and the model should show which failure forces it and who stays stuck. Revised: the child's stage now has the key child_stage, so that it cannot be confused with the wants the model holds for every person (the estimator read Laura's modeled wants as 'w…
lenses.source: An author-supplied talk, recorded 26 September 2026 (speaker not identified in this record): people move through three stages, wanting (the child), bartering (the adolescent) and standing (the adult); many get stuck bartering, and a more transactional modern world keeps them there.
lenses.trajectory: A crossing from bartering to standing usually needs a failure that bartering cannot survive: the reaction one performed for is withdrawn or turns out to be worthless. Staying in bartering means every later act is still a performance, even acts that look generous. A modern, transactional setting (likes, yields, appraisals) rewards bartering and so delays the crossing.

lenses.name: Who can switch it off
lenses.question: Who holds the off switch of {subject}: a person, an office or board, a charismatic founder, code and whoever holds its keys, or nobody?

answers.meaning: One named person can stop it.
An office acting by rules (Weber's rational-legal authority) can stop it.
A founder whose followers act on his word can stop or steer it.
It runs as code; only those holding its keys, or a coordinated majority, can stop it.
Nobody can switch it off.

lenses.why: Barbara's first question to Kieran, asked of the world: the works and the plant were switched off by boards; the Hart can be; the clearing by an office; the Sharehouse by its moderators; the stablecoin by nobody, which is why its failure could not be stopped once it started; the market by nobody. Joined with Weber's types of authority and a fourth this world adds, authority by code, it predicts where the story's powerlessness comes from and why the old institutions feel both oppressive and safe.
lenses.source: Barbara Ashby's question in part 1; Max Weber's traditional, rational-legal and charismatic authority, with authority by code added for this world.
lenses.trajectory: An era that moves its money from switches held by offices to switches held by nobody trades arbitrary power for unstoppable failure.

lenses.name: Wonder, appetite or anxiety
lenses.question: Is {subject} moved by wonder (wanting to see and understand how things are), appetite (wanting more of something: money, status, the rush), or anxiety (the fear of missing out, of being left behind)?

answers.meaning: Curiosity for its own sake: wanting to see the map past its edges, to understand how a thing works, with nothing to gain.
Wanting more of something: money, status, the rush of the number going up; curiosity turned into consumption.
The fear of missing out or being left behind: moving because others are moving.

lenses.why: The brief puts curiosity at the centre ('Human curiosity is powerful, and after years of monotony, they're tired enough to follow it'), and fear or love cannot see it: typing the twelve words in reads 31% neither. If curiosity is a process, the story's descent is wonder turning into appetite and then into anxiety, and the ending is wonder recovered without appetite (Kieran's unscripted questions on the last call, Barbara's lessons).
lenses.source: The supplied story premise; the old distinction between curiositas and studiositas (Augustine, Aquinas) and the modern psychology of fear of missing out.
lenses.trajectory: A life whose wonder becomes appetite and then anxiety has been captured by the thing it wanted to understand; recovering wonder without appetite is a way out.

nodes.title: Blind review: the character note and the ending note
nodes.text: Two notes outside the numbered findings were answered, model first (revision 23). 'A little kind to him': at the November 2021 peak Kieran now likes the number, opening the app only to look at it and feeling it in his shoulders like a warm bath (ev.kieran.likes_the_number; the wanting lens also reads his deposit move as wanting). 'The rebuild is frictionless': in October 2022 they have the worst row of their eight years about forty pounds he forgot to mention, she admits she has checked the joint account behind his back every day since August, and they add a CHECKED column to the spreadsheet that she ticks openly for a month and then forgets to (ev.kieran_laura.forty_pounds).

nodes.title: Blind review F2: how it was answered
nodes.text: Accepted the finding, not the suggested fix. Moving his own stake into the dollar would contradict the model, where his own money stays in the farm tokens (process kieran.stake_gbp; the states of 9 and 14 May 2022). The model now carries that path (revision 23, ev.kieran.own_stake_2022): about 45,000 in January, about 10,000 on 13 May, about 6,000 by mid-June, 5,200 sold into the joint account in September. The prose says so in parts 7, 8, 9 ('Of the deposit, about three hundred and forty pounds. Of mine, about six thousand.') and 11.
